name: Implicit Associations
description: People can show fast, automatic associative links between concepts and attributes even when those links are not available or acceptable in explicit self-report. In practice the term usually refers to relative association patterns inferred indirectly from tasks such as the Implicit Association Test.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to fairness, inclusive design, recommendation systems, moderation, measurement, and responsible-AI evaluation. Its value is mostly in understanding how automatic associations can shape interpretation and decision contexts; it is not a general-purpose interface law.
myth_risk_note: This pass's discovery did not surface the well-known, more critical meta-analyses that specifically challenge IAT predictive validity for actual discriminatory behavior (Oswald et al. 2013; Forscher et al. 2019/2021 on bias-change interventions) -- those papers are not in this entry's candidate pool, so they cannot be cited here, but their absence should not be read as their nonexistence. Even within what WAS found, Greenwald, Poehlman, Uhlmann & Banaji's (2009) own 122-report meta-analysis reports a modest mean r=.274 for predicting behavior/judgment/physiological outcomes, and Hofmann, Gawronski, Gschwendner, Le & Schmitt's (2005) meta-analysis of 126 studies finds only r=.24 correlation between implicit and explicit measures -- both consistent with genuine, substantial, and still-debated limits on the IAT's predictive power, not the strong hidden-belief-detector framing sometimes assumed in popular usage.
prevalence_note: A standard term in implicit-cognition and bias-measurement work, and increasingly relevant to fairness or responsible-AI discussions, but still more technical than the everyday product-design canon.

findings.description: The Implicit Association Test showed that relative response times in paired categorization tasks can reveal differential automatic associations between concepts and attributes, often diverging from explicit self-report.
findings.source_title: Measuring individual differences in implicit cognition: The implicit association test.
findings.source_venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
